clue.text: Adams' work a tall building? Not now I know

parts.note: the Shard is London's tallest skyscraper, near London Bridge

indicators.note: 'Not now' asks for the word now to be taken away from the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion
the letters to be removed, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone half-remembers a work by Adams about a skyscraper, then admits they no longer know it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes NOW from KNOW, leaving K. Richard Adams, author of Watership Down, also wrote this novel about a giant bear, the first of the bears that 7 down points to.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Adams wrote a 1974 novel of that title about a huge sacred bear, so it is one of his works.

clue.text: Covering? Having 7 I'm on guard

definitions.meaning: a hide or outer layer covers an animal's body
with the answer to 7 down's first word placed in front, it becomes the tall fur cap worn by Guards on sentry duty

explanation.surface: A bit of cover, and a speaker who says they are standing guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 down is BEAR WITH ME, so 'having 7' means having BEAR alongside: the bearskin is the tall black fur hat of the British Foot Guards, seen outside Buckingham Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is the natural outer layer of an animal, and a coat of paint or pastry can be one too.

clue.text: Any number of years old?

definitions.meaning: a child described as two years of age, or ten, or any figure: the word goes before that count

explanation.surface: A question about how many years makes someone old.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means elderly, and also precedes a stated age, as in 'a man of forty'.

clue.text: Take top job away from idle fellow in whom is the problem?

indicators.note: this says the next letters are placed inside the idle fellow

parts.note: a drone is a male bee that does no work, hence a lazy person

indicators.note: the word the is a problem, a puzzle to be worked out, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Removing a boss from office by blaming a lazy man who is himself the trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' makes ETH, which 'in whom is' places in the lazy fellow. The surface paints a boss deposed for being idle; a drone is the male bee that does no work.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove a monarch or leader from the throne is to strip them of the highest position.

clue.text: Finish off a US city where I could have 7

parts.note: a knockout ends a boxing match, abbreviated KO
LA is short for Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Someone means to finish off an American city, a place where they could put up with things.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 down is BEAR WITH ME: this animal could take BEAR after it, as in koala bear, though it is really a marsupial.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian marsupial is popularly called a koala bear, so it could be followed by the theme word.

clue.text: A bomb exploding round sticky stuff

indicators.note: a bomb going off blows things apart, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A bomb going off around some kind of glue or gooey mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploding' shuffles A BOMB into BAMBO, then O is added. 'sticky stuff' is not glue: it means material that gives sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Canes of this giant grass are used as garden sticks, so it is stuff that sticks are made from.

clue.text: Member in liquor, say

indicators.note: the limb sits inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a malt liquor, a kind of beer
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A limb dunked in strong drink, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: To claim something without proof is to assert or state it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: 10 wait while I'm accompanied by 1 across, 11 the 24, 17 or 28

definitions.meaning: with 10 across supplied, this reads as a polite request to be patient

definitions.text: I'm accompanied by 1 across, 11 the 24, 17 or 28
definitions.meaning: those answers make Shardik, Winnie the Pooh, Ted and Rupert, all famous bears, so the speaker has a bear alongside

explanation.surface: A request to wait politely, while the speaker is joined by a string of other answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 across is PLEASE. The second reading takes the phrase literally: a bear is with me. Shardik, Winnie the Pooh, Teddy and Rupert are fictional bears.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for asking someone to be patient, and literally means a bruin keeps me company.

clue.text: Proverbial king of Venice, perhaps, treating anemone with dye

indicators.note: treating a flower with dye alters it, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A Venetian ruler of legend is busy colouring a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'in the land of the blind, the one-eyed man is king'; Venice is the land of the blind because of Venetian blinds.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying crowns this figure king among the sightless, and Venetian blinds make Venice a land of blinds.

clue.text: Helium or argon, which could be angriest?

indicators.note: the letters of the next word could be rearranged into the answer

explanation.surface: A question of whether a gas such as helium could be the most furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which could be' rearranges ANGRIEST. These gases are famously unreactive, so the angriest is the last thing they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium and argon are examples of the noble gases, which barely react with other elements.

clue.text: Piano to let by request

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly
to lease property is to let it to a tenant

explanation.surface: A piano offered for rent on request.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the polite marker added when making a request, as in 'two coffees, if you would'.

clue.text: Local first in the Guardian for Churchill

indicators.note: the pub and the first sit inside the newspaper's pronoun

parts.note: a newspaper speaks of itself as we in its editorials
a pub, the local, is an inn
the figure 1 looks like the letter I

explanation.surface: A local pub gets the first mention in this newspaper's coverage of Churchill.
explanation.walkthrough: Winston Churchill was nicknamed this; it is also Winnie the Pooh, one of the bears of 7 down. The 'local' is British for one's nearest pub.
explanation.definitionFit: It was the affectionate nickname for Winston Churchill, a short form of his first name.

clue.text: Seceding Spooner's arousing a comment from an ass

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so two sounds are exchanged here

parts.note: waking someone is rousing them
a donkey's cry is a bray

explanation.surface: Someone splitting off from a group is woken by a donkey's noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the W of WAKING with the BR of A BRAY: 'braking a way' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakaway group secedes, so the phrase means leaving a union or federation.

clue.text: Seedsman embracing meal for member needs energy provider

indicators.note: the seedsman holds the next pieces inside him

parts.note: one who sows seed is a sower
tea is a light evening meal
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A seed merchant offering a meal to a member who needs something to fuel him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' wraps the seedsman round the meal and member. 'Member' suggests a limb, but it is a Member of Parliament; tea is a British name for an early evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam driving engines was the force behind railways and factories, so it supplies energy.

clue.text: Nasty turn for boat raised this way — it's usually mocked

parts.note: a boat that capsizes is said to turn turtle
so means in this manner
up means lifted, raised

explanation.surface: A boat capsizes and is righted by a method everyone laughs at.
explanation.walkthrough: Mock turtle soup is an imitation made from a calf's head, hence 'usually mocked'.
explanation.definitionFit: The dish is most often met as its imitation, mock turtle soup, so it is usually mocked.

clue.text: What they call us in the course of explosive competition

indicators.note: the phrase sits in the middle of the explosive

parts.note: TNT is trinitrotoluene, a high explosive
what people call us is our name

explanation.surface: A complaint about what people call us during a heated contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the course of' puts OUR NAME inside TNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of contests, as in tennis or chess, is a competition between many players.

clue.text: Sell old ship in custody of police

indicators.note: being held by the police means sitting inside them

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
Noah's ark is the ancient vessel of Genesis

explanation.surface: An old ship is to be sold after being seized by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in custody of' places the ark within the police. The Met is the usual short name for London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to promote and offer goods for sale.

clue.text: Bill's left off boring another boy

indicators.note: the bills are left off, removed from the end of the boring word

parts.note: something tedious is boring
an IOU is a written bill of debt; with the 's it gives IOUs

explanation.surface: Bill's not boring any more, unlike some other boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left off' removes the bills from the boring word. Bill is a boy's name in the surface, so 'another boy' follows; Ted is also Teddy, one of 7 down's bears.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a short form of Edward or Theodore, a boy's name beside Bill.

clue.text: Bird that can't fly — hence fly is to make milk?

parts.note: the emu is a flightless Australian bird

indicators.note: hence means away, so the following letters are sent off and rearranged

explanation.surface: A flightless bird reasons that it must instead fly to make milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hence' shuffles FLY IS into LSIFY. The question mark is because milk is an example of an emulsion, fat suspended in water.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk is a natural emulsion of fat droplets in water, so making it means creating an emulsion.

clue.text: I am not dialectical: having 7 I'm an aardvark

definitions.meaning: the dialect contraction ... stands for am not
with the answer to 7 down's first word after it, this makes the ...-bear, another name for the aardvark

explanation.surface: A speaker denies talking in dialect, then claims to be an aardvark.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 down is BEAR WITH ME, so 'having 7' adds BEAR. The aardvark is also called the ant-bear.
explanation.definitionFit: An't is an old dialect form of 'am not', and the ant-bear is the aardvark.

clue.text: Slippery creature gives manager MBE

indicators.note: something that gives bends out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A slippery manager is awarded an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives' rearranges MANAGER MBE. An MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: The African tree snake of this name is venomous and quick, so slippery suits it.

clue.text: Tree non-U, if non-U

indicators.note: the second non-U asks for the letter U to be taken away

parts.note: non-U is used of words judged common or lower-class, and popular means belonging to the common people

explanation.surface: A tree is deemed common if it is not upper-class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U' and 'non-U' were 1950s British labels for upper-class and not upper-class speech. 'if non-U' removes U from POPULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: This tall fast-growing tree of the willow family is often planted in lines.

clue.text: Male — no, males — with exterior that's friendly to a remarkable extent

indicators.note: the friendly word forms the outside, wrapping the rest

parts.note: pally means friendly
he is the male pronoun
taken as written
men are males

explanation.surface: A man correcting himself to men, with a friendly outward manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with exterior' wraps the friendly word round the rest. The surface stutters like someone correcting a slip, which hides that each word is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means extraordinarily, to a degree worth marvelling at.

clue.text: Each in the lead

definitions.meaning: read as two words, it means per person, as in ten pounds a head

explanation.surface: Every one of them is in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, it means per person; as one word it means in front of others.

clue.text: Ring up to show contempt

indicators.note: in a down clue, up reads the ring from the bottom

parts.note: a hoop is a ring

explanation.surface: Phoning someone to show disdain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses HOOP. Also Winnie the Pooh, a 7 down bear.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is uttered to express scorn, as in pooh-poohing an idea.

clue.text: I'm in hospital: having 7 I'm Arcturus

definitions.meaning: a room of beds in a hospital
with the answer to 7 down's first word in front, this makes bearward, keeper of the bear, the meaning of the star's Greek name

explanation.surface: A patient says they are in hospital and also a bright star.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 down is BEAR WITH ME, so 'having 7' adds BEAR. Arcturus is Greek for guardian of the bear, as it follows the Great Bear.
explanation.definitionFit: A division of a hospital, and the second half of bearward, the bear's keeper Arcturus is named for.

clue.text: Jumper, maybe: having 7 I'll be a tiger moth

definitions.meaning: a jumper is a sweater, often knitted from fleece

definitions.text: having 7 I'll be a tiger moth
definitions.meaning: with the answer to 7 down's first word after it, this gives the ... bear, the hairy caterpillar of the tiger moth

explanation.surface: A sweater announcing it will grow into a moth.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is British for a sweater. 7 down is BEAR WITH ME, so 'having 7' adds BEAR: woolly bear is the tiger moth caterpillar.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted pullover is often called by this word, and the woolly bear caterpillar becomes a tiger moth.

clue.text: Half-asleep state of most rodents with much of home in water

indicators.note: the rodents and the home go inside the water

parts.note: the sea is a large body of water

indicators.note: most of the rodents means dropping their last letter

parts.note: mice are small rodents

indicators.note: much of the word home is its middle, without the ends

explanation.surface: A drowsy state brought on by too many rodents in a house that is flooded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most' drops the last of the rodents, 'much of' keeps the core of home, and 'in' sets both inside the water. Semicoma is a medical term for a light stupor.
explanation.definitionFit: A partial coma is a stupor short of full unconsciousness, so the sufferer is half asleep.

clue.text: Prince gets by when in the groove

indicators.note: the by sits inside the groove

parts.note: a rut is a groove worn in a road
per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: A prince gets by while stuck in a rut.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Rupert of the Rhine was a Royalist general; Rupert is also the cartoon bear in the Daily Express, one of 7 down's bears.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Rupert of the Rhine, nephew of Charles I, led the Royalist cavalry in the English Civil War.

clue.text: Kept your feet out of water? Your dinner starts with hors d'oeuvre

definitions.text: Kept your feet out of water?

indicators.note: an oeuvre is a body of work, and the letters are worked into a new order
the starts of the words are their first letters

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A diner kept their feet dry while the meal began with a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: Take Y and D from 'Your dinner', add HORS D, and 'oeuvre' (works) rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means having crossed without wetting one's shoes, so a person so described kept their feet dry.
